newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen falls sharply on rate rise concerns.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen falls sharply on rate rise concerns.

text.p: Key December three-month euroyen deposit rate futures on TIFFE were sharply down by midday on Friday on worries over an interest rate rise, traders said.
The December contract ended the morning down 0.08 at 98.84, after falling as low as 98.82 earlier in the session.
"Selling pressure intensified on growing worries about a possible interest rate rise. A stronger yen and weaker stocks provided little support," said a city bank trader.
A sharp fall in Japanese government bond futures also weighed on euroyen futures, traders said. Key June JGB futures ended the morning down 1.30 at 122.75.
Traders said sentiment soured after a senior Finance Ministry official said on Thursday that the yen may strengthen to 103 yen to the dollar.

The remarks by Eisuke Sakakibara, director general of MOF's international finance bureau, led to speculation that MOF would be willing to see an interest rate rise to prevent the yen from weakening further, traders said.
Foreign players' selling this morning was more aggressive than domestic players, a trust bank trader said.
The December contract, however, may be supported at 98.80 for the time being, traders said.

"Suppose the overnight rate rises by 25 basis points, the appropriate level of three-month interest rates would be around 1.1 to 1.2 percent judging from past experience. Hence, 98.80 for the benchmark euroyen futures seems to be a fair level," said the city bank trader.
In the interbank money market, key unsecured overnight call money was mainly traded at 0.46 percent, down from Thursday's weighted average of 0.49 percent, traders said.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) drained a net 200 billion yen in its regular money market operation, leaving the market in surplus by about 120 billion yen.
The overnight rate had been expected to fall on Friday due to weekend factors, money traders said.
No new certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued on Friday morning, money traders said. Key three-month CDs were offered at 0.57 percent.
One-month CDs were offered at 0.54 percent and two-month CDs at 0.55 percent. All CD rates were flat from Thursday.
Interest rate swap (IRS) rates were sharply higher following the fall in JGB futures.
Ten-year IRS rates were quoted at 3.09/3.13 percent by midday, up from 2.96/3.00 percent late on Thursday.
Five-year IRS rates were quoted at 2.24/2.28 percent, up from 2.10/14 percent late on Thursday.
Seven-year IRS rates were at 2.70/2.74 percent, up from 2.56/2.60 percent the previous day.
